search_text.description:
Searches for a text substring within project files.
Use this tool for fast literal text search with match coordinates. It is the first choice; reach for search_regex only when a pattern is required.
Results include match coordinates when available (1-based line and column, end exclusive).

Examples:
- Find every use of an error message: q="connection refused"
- Limit the search to production code: paths=["src/**", "!**/test/**"]
- Find every Kotlin build file: paths=["**/*.gradle.kts"]

params.q: Text to search for. A plain substring, not a pattern. Example: "readText"
params.paths: Glob patterns relative to the project root. Examples: ["src/**", "!**/test/**"], ["**/*.kt"], ["foo/"]. Supports '!' excludes. Trailing '/' expands to '**'. Patterns without '/' are treated as '**/pattern'. Empty strings are ignored.
params.limit: Maximum number of results to return. Default: 1000.

search_regex.description:
Searches for regular expression matches within project files.
Use this tool when a pattern is required, for example a call site of the form foo(...) on one line. Prefer search_text for a literal substring.
Results include match coordinates when available (1-based line and column, end exclusive).

Examples:
- Find single-line method calls: q="println\\(.*\\)"
- Find TODO comments in test files: paths=["**/test/**"], q="TODO"
- Find logging calls across the project: q="logger\\.(info|warn|error)"

params.q: Regular expression to search for. Examples: "println\\(.*\\)", "TODO", "logger\\.(info|warn|error)".
params.paths: Glob patterns relative to the project root. Examples: ["src/**", "!**/test/**"], ["**/*.kt"], ["foo/"]. Supports '!' excludes. Trailing '/' expands to '**'. Patterns without '/' are treated as '**/pattern'. Empty strings are ignored.
params.limit: Maximum number of results to return. Default: 1000.

search_symbol.description:
Searches for symbols: classes, methods, and fields.
Use this tool for semantic lookup by identifier fragments. It is faster and more precise than text search when you know a name.
Results include match coordinates when available (1-based line and column, end exclusive).
For call graph questions, use this tool to locate the target symbol, then pass the fully qualified callable name to analyze_calls.

Examples:
- Locate a class by name fragment: q="ExtractMethodPipeline"
- Locate a method: q="suggestSafeMethodNames"
- Widen the search when nothing is found: q="PsiDocumentManager", include_external=true

params.q: Symbol query text. An identifier fragment, not a wildcard pattern. Example: "ExtractMethodPipeline".
params.paths: Glob patterns relative to the project root. Examples: ["src/**"], ["**/*.java"]. Supports '!' excludes.
params.include_external: Whether to include SDK and library symbols. Disabled by default. Try it when the project search found nothing suitable.
params.limit: Maximum number of results to return. Default: 1000.

rename_refactoring.description:
Renames a symbol (variable, function, class, etc.) in the specified file.
Use this tool to perform rename refactoring operations.

The `rename_refactoring` tool is a powerful, context-aware utility. Unlike a simple text search-and-replace, it understands the code's structure and will intelligently update ALL references to the specified symbol throughout the project, ensuring code integrity and preventing broken references. It is ALWAYS the preferred method for renaming programmatic symbols.

Examples:
- Rename a method and update all callers: pathInProject="src/main/java/Foo.java", symbolName="oldName", newName="newName"
- Rename a class: The tool updates imports, extends clauses, and all usages across the project
- Rename a local variable: Updates all references within the method scope

params.pathInProject: Relative path to the file from the project's root directory. Example: "src/api/controllers/userController.java"
params.symbolName: Exact, case-sensitive name of the existing symbol to be renamed. Example: "getUserData"
params.newName: New, case-sensitive name for the symbol. Example: "fetchUserData"

move_method.description:
Moves a Java method from its containing class to a target class, updating all call sites to reference the method in its new location.

The tool auto-dispatches based on the method's modifiers:
- Static methods are moved as static members of the target class.
- Instance methods are moved to the target class, taking the target-typed variable as its receiver (`this`). The variable is auto-detected (the first method parameter or field whose type resolves to the target class) or selected explicitly via `targetVariableName`.

Returns a structured result with success, the updated usages count, and the list of changed files. When the refactoring detects conflicts (e.g. member name clash in the target class, inaccessible members), nothing is changed and success is false with the conflict descriptions.

Examples:
- Move a static utility method: pathInProject="src/Foo.java", methodName="helper", targetClass="com.example.Bar"
- Move an instance method onto a field: pathInProject="src/Order.java", methodName="process", targetClass="com.example.Processor", targetVariableName="processor"
- Move with visibility change: pathInProject="src/Service.java", methodName="internalHelper", targetClass="com.example.Utils", visibility="private"

params.pathInProject: Relative path to the Java file from the project root
params.methodName: Exact name of the method to move
params.targetClass: Fully-qualified name of the destination class. Example: "org.acme.Bar"
params.visibility: Visibility applied to the moved method: "public", "protected", "private" or "package" (package-private). Default: "public"
params.targetVariableName: For instance methods: name of the parameter or field in the source class that receives the moved method. Defaults to auto-detection.
params.parameterTypes: Optional parameter types to disambiguate overloaded methods. Example: ["String", "int"]

extract_method.description:
Extracts the code fragment at the given line/column range of a Java file into a new method, replacing the selection with a call site (IntelliJ Extract Method refactoring).

The range uses 1-based line and column coordinates, matching the numbered output of `read_file` and the coordinates accepted by `get_symbol_info`. `endColumn` is inclusive; when omitted, the selection extends to the end of `endLine`.

Returns a structured result with success, the new method's name, signature and code, and the list of changed files. When the fragment cannot be extracted (e.g. multiple output variables, broken control flow), nothing is changed and success is false with the reason in message.

Examples:
- Extract lines 10-15 into a named method: pathInProject="src/Foo.java", startLine=10, endLine=15, methodName="processData"
- Extract with column precision: pathInProject="src/Bar.java", startLine=20, startColumn=5, endLine=25, endColumn=40
- Extract and let IntelliJ suggest a name: pathInProject="src/Service.java", startLine=50, endLine=60

params.pathInProject: Relative path to the Java file from the project root
params.startLine: 1-based line number of the first selected line
params.startColumn: 1-based column number of the first selected character (default: 1)
params.endLine: 1-based line number of the last selected line
params.endColumn: 1-based column number of the last selected character, inclusive (default: end of line)
params.methodName: Name for the extracted method. If omitted, a safe name is suggested automatically.
params.targetClass: Fully-qualified name of the class the method should be placed in. Defaults to the innermost enclosing class of the selection.

introduce_parameter.description:
Replaces a local variable with a new method parameter, updating all call sites of the method in the project (IntelliJ Introduce Parameter refactoring).

The local declaration is removed and every occurrence in the body becomes a reference to the new parameter. When the method overrides a method from the project, the parameter is also introduced into the deepest super method so the whole hierarchy stays consistent.

Returns a structured result with success, the new parameter's name and type, the resulting method signature, the number of replaced occurrences, and the list of changed files. When the variable or method cannot be resolved, or the refactoring detects conflicts (e.g. an inaccessible initializer at some call site), nothing is changed and success is false with the reason.

Examples:
- Turn a local variable into a parameter: pathInProject="src/Foo.java", variableName="tempValue"
- Introduce in a specific overloaded method: pathInProject="src/Service.java", variableName="config", methodName="init", parameterTypes=["Properties"]
- Introduce in an override hierarchy: The parameter propagates to the deepest super method automatically

params.pathInProject: Relative path to the Java file from the project root
params.variableName: Exact name of the local variable to replace with the new parameter
params.methodName: Optional name of the method declaring the variable, to disambiguate when several methods declare a variable with the same name
params.parameterTypes: Optional method parameter types to disambiguate overloaded methods. Example: ["String", "int"]
params.replaceAllOccurrences: Replace every occurrence of the variable in the method body (default true). False is accepted only when the variable is referenced exactly once.
params.position: Index of the new parameter in the method signature (default: appended at the end; currently only that default position is supported)

pull_up_method.description:
Pulls a Java method up from its containing class into a superclass, updating all references with it (IntelliJ Pull Members Up refactoring).

When `makeAbstract` is set the superclass keeps an abstract declaration and the implementation stays in the source class (now overriding the abstract one). The default (false) removes the member from the source class entirely.

When the method depends on members of its own class that are not being pulled up, the refactoring is aborted with success=false listing the offending members - nothing is changed.

Returns a structured result with success, the moved members, the updated-usage count, and the list of changed files.

Examples:
- Pull a method to the direct superclass: pathInProject="src/Child.java", methodName="doWork", targetClass="com.example.Parent"
- Pull and keep abstract in superclass: pathInProject="src/ConcreteImpl.java", methodName="execute", makeAbstract=true
- Pull to a specific interface: pathInProject="src/ServiceImpl.java", methodName="process", targetClass="com.example.Processor"

params.pathInProject: Relative path to the Java file from the project root
params.methodName: Exact name of the method to pull up
params.parameterTypes: Optional parameter types to disambiguate overloaded methods. Example: ["String", "int"]
params.targetClass: Fully-qualified name of the destination superclass; defaults to the direct superclass of the method's containing class
params.makeAbstract: When true, the superclass receives an abstract declaration and the implementation stays in the source class. Default: false.

push_down_method.description:
Pushes a Java method from a superclass into one or all of its direct subclasses, updating references (IntelliJ Push Members Down refactoring).

When `targetClass` is omitted the method is pushed into ALL direct subclasses and the declaration in the superclass is kept as `abstract <sig>;`, so the class hierarchy stays intact. If a single `targetClass` is given, the method moves entirely: the subclass receives a real implementation and nothing abstract remains in the source class.

Returns a structured result with success, the source and destination classes, the count of references rewritten, whether the superclass kept an abstract declaration, and the list of changed files.

Examples:
- Push to all subclasses (keeps abstract in source): pathInProject="src/Parent.java", methodName="templateMethod"
- Push to a specific subclass: pathInProject="src/AbstractHandler.java", methodName="handle", targetClass="com.example.ConcreteHandler"
- Push an overloaded method: pathInProject="src/Base.java", methodName="process", parameterTypes=["String"], targetClass="com.example.Derived"

params.pathInProject: Relative path to the Java file from the project root
params.methodName: Exact name of the method to push down
params.parameterTypes: Optional parameter types to disambiguate overloaded methods. Example: ["String", "int"]
params.targetClass: Fully-qualified name of a single destination subclass; when omitted, ALL direct subclasses receive the method and the source keeps an abstract declaration

inline_method.description:
Inlines a Java method into all of its call sites, replacing each call with the method body (IntelliJ Inline Method refactoring), optionally removing the now-empty method declaration.

By default every call site in the project is inlined. Set `inlineThisOnly` to inline a single invocation instead; because there is no cursor in this context, this requires the method to have exactly one call site in the project.

Returns a structured result with success, the number of inlined usages, whether the method declaration was deleted, and the list of changed files. When the method cannot be inlined (recursive, abstract/native, or a call site that would need interactive conflict resolution), nothing is changed and success is false with the reason.

Examples:
- Inline all usages and delete the method: pathInProject="src/Foo.java", methodName="helper", deleteMethod=true
- Inline a single call site: pathInProject="src/Bar.java", methodName="utility", inlineThisOnly=true
- Inline but keep the method: pathInProject="src/Utils.java", methodName="format", deleteMethod=false

params.pathInProject: Relative path to the Java file from the project root
params.methodName: Exact name of the method to inline
params.parameterTypes: Optional parameter types to disambiguate overloaded methods. Example: ["String", "int"]
params.inlineThisOnly: Inline only the single existing call site instead of all usages. Requires exactly one call site in the project. Default: false.
params.deleteMethod: Remove the method declaration after inlining all usages. Default: true. Ignored when inlineThisOnly is set.

safe_delete.description:
Safely deletes a code symbol (class, method, field, parameter or local variable) declared in the specified Java file, after verifying that every usage in the project can be resolved by the IntelliJ Safe Delete refactoring.

All usages of the symbol are searched project-wide through the language's Safe Delete delegate. Usages inside the deleted element itself, or inside code that is deleted along with it, are handled automatically.

If any usage lives in code that is NOT being deleted, or the deletion would normally raise a confirmation dialog (unsafe references, overriding implementations, callers of a deleted class, parameter hierarchy), nothing is changed and success is false with the reason.

Returns a structured result with success, the detected symbol kind, the number of usages found and updated, the deleted file(s), and all changed files.

Examples:
- Delete an unused method: pathInProject="src/Foo.java", symbolName="oldMethod"
- Delete a class: pathInProject="src/Bar.java", symbolName="Bar", kind="class"
- Delete a field: pathInProject="src/Entity.java", symbolName="deprecatedField", kind="field"

params.pathInProject: Relative path to the Java file from the project root
params.symbolName: Exact name of the symbol to delete
params.kind: Optional element kind to disambiguate: "class", "method", "field", "parameter" or "local". Default: auto - the first matching element of any supported kind.
